account: On 26 August 2017 Breakthrough Listen made a five-hour, 400-terabyte observation with the Green Bank Telescope. Conventional algorithms found 21 bursts in these data. Gerry Zhang, a University of California, Berkeley graduate student, built a convolutional neural network with Breakthrough Listen collaborators to search the same data again. The network found 72 previously undetected pulses from the repeating fast radio burst FRB 121102. The team reported the combined 93 pulses, including 45 within the first 30 minutes, in a peer-reviewed Astrophysical Journal paper (Zhang et al. 2018). The team used the pulses to search for periodicity. On 10 September 2018 the Green Bank Observatory announced the result. The detections came from a re-analysis of the team's own data. In November 2019 researchers at Nanjing University with no tie to Breakthrough Listen used the 93 pulses as the largest sample of FRB 121102 in their own analysis of burst statistics. They did not re-check the detections. In a Nature Astronomy paper published on 19 October 2023, astronomers at the University of Amsterdam and ASTRON, joined by Breakthrough Listen's Vishal Gajjar, searched the first 30 minutes of the same observation again with a different method. They re-detected all 18 bursts that the classical search had found in that span and 12 pulses that only the neural network had found. They report that the 16 network candidates that they missed were faint pulses whose astrophysical nature is unclear. The rest of the observation was not searched again. No source reports a re-detection by a group without a Breakthrough Listen author.

ai_role.statement: The CNN flagged 72 pulses in data that a classical search had already processed, where that search had found 21. The authors vetted the detections, and peer reviewers accepted them. In 2023 a mostly separate team that includes one Breakthrough Listen author searched the first 30 minutes again with a different method; it re-detected 12 pulses that only the CNN had found and missed 16 faint CNN candidates.

fields.headline: Neural network finds 72 missed pulses from a repeating fast radio burst
fields.title: Convolutional neural network finds 72 previously undetected pulses from fast radio burst FRB 121102 in Green Bank Telescope data

fields.account: On 26 August 2017 Breakthrough Listen made a five-hour, 400-terabyte observation with the Green Bank Telescope. Conventional algorithms found 21 bursts in these data. Gerry Zhang, a University of California, Berkeley graduate student, built a convolutional neural network with Breakthrough Listen collaborators to search the same data again. The network found 72 previously undetected pulses from the repeating fast radio burst FRB 121102. The team reported the combined 93 pulses, including 45 within the first 30 minutes, in a peer-reviewed Astrophysical Journal paper (Zhang et al. 2018). The team used the pulses to search for periodicity. On 10 September 2018 the Green Bank Observatory announced the result. The detections came from a re-analysis of the team's own data. In November 2019 researchers at Nanjing University with no tie to Breakthrough Listen used the 93 pulses as the largest sample of FRB 121102 in their own analysis of burst statistics. They did not re-check the detections. In a Nature Astronomy paper published on 19 October 2023, astronomers at the University of Amsterdam and ASTRON, joined by Breakthrough Listen's Vishal Gajjar, searched the first 30 minutes of the same observation again with a different method. They re-detected all 18 bursts that the classical search had found in that span and 12 pulses that only the neural network had found. They report that the 16 network candidates that they missed were faint pulses whose astrophysical nature is unclear. The rest of the observation was not searched again. No source reports a re-detection by a group without a Breakthrough Listen author.

purpose: Built to detect pulses from fast radio bursts that classical search algorithms miss in Breakthrough Listen radio data. The 72 new pulses are the result that it was built to produce.

ratings.reason: Breakthrough Listen recovered 72 additional bursts from an existing 400-terabyte Green Bank dataset without new telescope time.
